Title: Set 'Account lockout threshold' to '5 invalid logon attempt(s)'
Description: 1.1.1.1 Set 'Account lockout threshold' to '5 invalid logon attempt(s)'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines the number of failed logon attempts before a lock occurs.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Account lockout threshold' is set to 5 invalid attempts.

Title: Set 'Account lockout duration' to '15 or more minute(s)'
Description: 1.1.1.2 Set 'Account lockout duration' to '15 or more minute(s)'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines the length of time that must pass before a locked account is unlocked and a
user can try to log on again.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Account lockout duration' is set to a minimum of 15 minutes.

Title: Set 'Reset account lockout counter after' to '15 minute(s)'
Description: 1.1.1.3 Set 'Reset account lockout counter after' to '15 minute(s)'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines the length of time before the Account lockout threshold resets to zero.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to a minimum of 15 minutes.

Title: Set 'Minimum password length' to '14 or more character(s)'
Description: 1.1.1.4 Set 'Minimum password length' to '14 or more character(s)'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines the least number of characters that make up a password for a user account.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Minimum password length' is set to a minimum of 14 characters.

Title: Set 'Enforce password history' to '24 or more password(s)'
Description: 1.1.1.5 Set 'Enforce password history' to '24 or more password(s)'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines the number of renewed, unique passwords that have to be associated with a user
account before you can reuse an old password.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Enforce password history' is set to a minimum of 24 passwords.

Title: Set 'Password must meet complexity requirements' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.1.6 Set 'Password must meet complexity requirements' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting checks all new passwords to ensure that they meet basic requirements for strong passwords.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Password must meet complexity requirements' is set to a minimum of 24 passwords.

Title: Set 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.1.7 Set 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether the operating system stores passwords in a way that uses reversible
encryption, which provides support for application protocols that require knowledge of the user's password
for authentication purposes.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Store passwords using reversible encryption' is disabled.

Title: Set 'Minimum password age' to '1 or more day(s)'
Description: 1.1.1.8 Set 'Minimum password age' to '1 or more day(s)'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines the number of days that you must use a password before you can change it.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure minimum password age is set to a minimum of 1 day.

Title: Set 'Maximum password age' to '60 or fewer days'
Description: 1.1.1.9 Set 'Maximum password age' to '60 or fewer days'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting defines how long a user can use their password before it expires.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'maximum password age' is set to a minimum of 60 days.

This policy setting creates a default system access control list (SACL) for system objects such as
mutexes (mutual exclusive), events, semaphores, and MS-DOS devices, and causes access to these system objects
to be audited.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Audit the access of global system objects' is disabled.

Title: Configure 'DCOM: Machine Launch Restrictions in Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) syntax'
Description: 1.1.3.3.1 Configure 'DCOM: Machine Launch Restrictions in Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) syntax'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which users or groups might launch or activate DCOM applications remotely or locally.

NOTE: Update MACHINE_LAUNCH_PRIV with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'DCOM: Machine Launch Restrictions in Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) syntax' is set to your organization's security requirements.

Title: Configure DCOM: Machine Access Restrictions in Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) syntax
Description: 1.1.3.3.2 Configure DCOM: Machine Access Restrictions in Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) syntax
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which users or groups might access DCOM application remotely or locally.

NOTE: Update MACHINE_ACCESS_PRIV with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'DCOM: Machine Access Restrictions in Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) syntax' is set to your organization's security requirements.

Title: Configure 'Devices: Allow undock without having to log on'
Description: 1.1.3.4.1 Configure 'Devices: Allow undock without having to log on'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether a portable computer can be undocked if the user does not log on to the system.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Devices: Allow undock without having to log on' is set to your organization's security requirements

Title: Configure 'Devices: Restrict floppy access to locally logged-on user only'
Description: 1.1.3.4.2 Configure 'Devices: Restrict floppy access to locally logged-on user only'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether removable floppy media are accessible to both local and remote
users simultaneously.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Devices: Restrict floppy access to locally logged-on user only' is set to your organization's security requirements.

Title: Set 'Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media' to 'Administrators and Interactive Users'
Description: 1.1.3.4.3 Set 'Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media' to 'Administrators and Interactive Users'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines who is allowed to format and eject removable media.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media' is set to administrators.

Title: Configure 'Devices: Restrict CD-ROM access to locally loggedon user only'
Description: 1.1.3.4.4 Configure 'Devices: Restrict CD-ROM access to locally loggedon user only'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether a CD-ROM is accessible to both local and remote users simultaneously.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Devices: Restrict CD-ROM access to locally logged-on user only' is set to your organization's security requirements

Title: Configure 'Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers'
Description: 1.1.3.4.5 Configure 'Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers'
Info / Rationale: It is feasible for a attacker to disguise a Trojan horse program as a printer driver.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers' is set to enabled.

Title: Set 'Domain member: Require strong (Windows 2000 or later) session key' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.5.1 Set 'Domain member: Require strong (Windows 2000 or later) session key' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
When this policy setting is enabled, a secure channel can only be established with domain controllers that
are capable of encrypting secure channel data with a strong (128-bit) session key.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Domain member: Require strong (Windows 2000 or later) session key' is enabled.

Title: Set 'Domain member: Digitally sign secure channel data (when possible)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.5.2 Set 'Domain member: Digitally sign secure channel data (when possible)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether a domain member should attempt to negotiate whether all secure channel
traffic that it initiates must be digitally signed.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Domain member: Digitally sign secure channel data (when possible)' is enabled.

Title: Set 'Domain member: Digitally encrypt secure channel data (when possible)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.5.3 Set 'Domain member: Digitally encrypt secure channel data (when possible)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether a domain member should attempt to negotiate encryption for all secure
channel traffic that it initiates.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Domain member: Digitally encrypt secure channel data (when possible)' is enabled.

Title: Set 'Domain member: Maximum machine account password age' to '30 or fewer day(s)'
Description: 1.1.3.5.4 Set 'Domain member: Maximum machine account password age' to '30 or fewer day(s)'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines the maximum allowable age for a computer account password.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Domain member: Maximum machine account password age' is set to a maximum of 30 days.

Title: Set 'Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.5.5 Set 'Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether all secure channel traffic that is initiated by the domain member
must be signed or encrypted.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always)' is set to enabled.

Title: Set 'Domain member: Disable machine account password changes' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.5.6 Set 'Domain member: Disable machine account password changes' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether a domain member can periodically change its computer account password.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Domain member: Disable machine account password changes' is disabled.

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Machine account lockout threshold' to 10 or fewer invalid logon attempts
Description: 1.1.3.6.1 Set 'Interactive logon: Machine account lockout threshold' to 10 or fewer invalid logon attempts
Info / Rationale: This security setting determines the number of failed logon attempts that causes the machine to be locked out.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Machine account lockout threshold' is set to 10 or fewer invalid logon attempts

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Smart card removal behavior' to 'Lock Workstation'
Description: 1.1.3.6.2 Set 'Interactive logon: Smart card removal behavior' to 'Lock Workstation'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines what happens when the smart card for a logged-on user is removed from
the smart card reader.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Smart card removal behavior' is set to lock the workstation.

Title: Configure 'Interactive logon: Require smart card'
Description: 1.1.3.6.3 Configure 'Interactive logon: Require smart card'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines if a user is required log on to a computer with a smart card.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Require smart card' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'startup (minutes)' to '10 or more minute(s)'
Description: 1.1.3.6.3 Set 'startup (minutes)' to '10 or more minute(s)'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines the amount of time before previously scheduled Automatic Update installations
will proceed after system startup.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure ''startup (minutes)' is set to '10 or more minute(s)'

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Do not display last user name' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.6.4 Set 'Interactive logon: Do not display last user name' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether the account name of the last user to log on to the client computers in your
organization will be displayed in each computer's respective Windows logon screen.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Do not display last user name' is enabled.

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache (in case domain controller is not available)' to '4 or fewer logon(s)'
Description: 1.1.3.6.5 Set 'Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache (in case domain controller is not available)' to '4 or fewer logon(s)'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether a user can log on to a Windows domain using cached account information.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache (in case domain controller is not available)' is set to 4 or fewer logons.

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Require Domain Controller authentication to unlock workstation' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.6.6 Set 'Interactive logon: Require Domain Controller authentication to unlock workstation' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: Logon information is required to unlock a locked computer.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Require Domain Controller authentication to unlock workstation' is disabled.

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Prompt user to change password before expiration' to '14 or more day(s)'
Description: 1.1.3.6.7 Set 'Interactive logon: Prompt user to change password before expiration' to '14 or more day(s)'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines how far in advance users are warned that their password will expire.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Prompt user to change password before expiration' is set to a minimum of 14 days.

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.6.8 Set 'Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether users must press CTRL+ALT+DEL before they log on.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL' is disabled.

Title: Configure 'Interactive logon: Message text for users attempting to log on'
Description: 1.1.3.6.9 Configure 'Interactive logon: Message text for users attempting to log on'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting specifies a text message that displays to users when they log on.

NOTE: Update LOGON_TEXT with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Message text for users attempting to log on' is set to your organization's security requirements.
Value Data: All activities performed on this system will be monitored.

Title: Set 'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit' to '900 or fewer seconds'
Description: 1.1.3.6.10 Set 'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit' to '900 or fewer seconds'
Info / Rationale:
Windows notices inactivity of a logon session, and if the amount of inactive time exceeds the inactivity limit,
then the screen saver will run, locking the session.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit' to '900 or fewer seconds' is set to a maximum of 900 seconds (15 minutes).

Title: Configure 'Interactive logon: Message title for users attempting to log on'
Description: 1.1.3.6.11 Configure 'Interactive logon: Message title for users attempting to log on'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows text to be specified in the title bar of the window that users see when they log on to the system.

NOTE: Update LOGON_CAPTION with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Message title for users attempting to log on' is set to your organization's security requirements.

Title: Configure 'Interactive logon: Display user information when the session is locked'
Description: 1.1.3.6.12 Configure 'Interactive logon: Display user information when the session is locked'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether the account name of the last user to log on to the client computers in your organization
can display in each computer's respective Windows logon screen.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Interactive logon: Display user information when the session is locked' is set to your organization's security requirements.

Title: Set 'Microsoft network client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.7.1 Set 'Microsoft network client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale:
Disable this policy setting to prevent the SMB redirector from sending plaintext passwords during authentication
to third-party SMB servers that do not support password encryption.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers' is set to disabled.

Title: Set 'Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.7.2 Set 'Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether packet signing is required by the SMB client component.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always)' is set to enabled.

Title: Set 'Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (if server agrees)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.7.3 Set 'Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (if server agrees)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether the SMB client will attempt to negotiate SMB packet signing.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (if server agrees)' is set to enabled.

Title: Set 'Microsoft network server: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.8.1 Set 'Microsoft network server: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether to disconnect users who are connected to the local computer outside
their user account's valid logon hours.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network server: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire' is enabled.

Title: Set 'Microsoft network server: Amount of idle time required before suspending session' to '15 or fewer minute(s)'
Description: 1.1.3.8.2 Set 'Microsoft network server: Amount of idle time required before suspending session' to '15 or fewer minute(s)'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows you to specify the amount of continuous idle time that must pass in an SMB session
before the session is suspended because of inactivity.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network server: Amount of idle time required before suspending session' is set to a maximum of 15 minutes.

Title: Set 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (if client agrees)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.8.3 Set 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (if client agrees)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines if the server side SMB service is able to sign SMB packets if it is requested to do so by a
client that attempts to establish a connection.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (if client agrees)' is enabled.

Title: Set 'Microsoft network server: Server SPN target name validation level' to 'Accept if provided by client'
Description: 1.1.3.8.4 Set 'Microsoft network server: Server SPN target name validation level' to 'Accept if provided by client'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting controls the level of validation a computer with shared folders or printers (the server) performs
on the service principal name (SPN) that is provided by the client computer when it establishes a session using the
server message block (SMB) protocol.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network server: Server SPN target name validation level' is set to 'Accept if provided by client'

Title: Set 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.8.5 Set 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines if the server side SMB service is required to perform SMB packet signing.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' is set to enabled.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (AutoShareWks) Enable Administrative Shares (recommended except for highly secure environments)'
Description: 1.1.3.9.1 Configure 'MSS: (AutoShareWks) Enable Administrative Shares (recommended except for highly secure environments)'
Info / Rationale:
This entry appears as MSS: (AutoShareWks) Enable Administrative Shares
(recommended except for highly secure environments) in the SCE.
Solution / Remediation: Configure this setting in a manner that is consistent with the security and operational requirements of your organization.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation) Enable the computer to stop generating 8.3 style filenames'
Description: 1.1.3.9.2 Configure 'MSS: (NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation) Enable the computer to stop generating 8.3 style filenames'
Info / Rationale:
The registry value entry NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation was added to the template file in the
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\ registry key. The entry appears as
MSS: (NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation) Enable the computer to stop generating 8.3 style filenames in the SCE.
Solution / Remediation: Configure this setting in a manner that is consistent with the security and operational requirements of your organization.

Title: Set 'MSS: (AutoAdminLogon) Enable Automatic Logon (not recommended)' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.9.3 Set 'MSS: (AutoAdminLogon) Enable Automatic Logon (not recommended)' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: This setting is separate from the Welcome screen feature in Windows XP and Windows Vista.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure AutoAdminLogon is disabled.

Title: Set 'MSS: (WarningLevel) Percentage threshold for the security event log at which the system will generate a warning' to '<= 0.9'
Description: 1.1.3.9.4 Set 'MSS: (WarningLevel) Percentage threshold for the security event log at which the system will generate a warning' to '<= 0.9'
Info / Rationale:
Set 'MSS: (WarningLevel) Percentage threshold for the security event log at which the system will generate a warning' to '0.9 or less'
This setting can generate a security audit in the Security event log when the log reaches a user-defined threshold.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure WarningLevel is set to 90 percent.

Title: Set 'MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)' to 'Highest protection'
Description: 1.1.3.9.5 Set 'MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)' to 'Highest protection'
Info / Rationale:
Set 'MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)' to 'Highest protection, source routing is completely disabled'
IP source routing is a mechanism that allows the sender to determine the IP route that a datagram should take
through the network.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure DisableIPSourceRouting is set to a value of Highest protection, source routing is completely disabled.

Title: Set 'MSS: (AutoReboot) Allow Windows to automatically restart after a system crash' to 'Not Defined'
Description: 1.1.3.9.6 Set 'MSS: (AutoReboot) Allow Windows to automatically restart after a system crash' to 'Not Defined'
Info / Rationale:
Set 'MSS: (AutoReboot) Allow Windows to automatically restart after a system crash (recommended except for highly secure environments)' to 'Not Defined'
This entry appears as MSS: (AutoReboot) Allow Windows to automatically restart after a system crash.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure AutoReboot is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (TcpMaxDataRetransmissions) How many times unacknowledged data is retransmitted (3 recommended, 5 is default)'
Description: 1.1.3.9.7 Configure 'MSS: (TcpMaxDataRetransmissions) How many times unacknowledged data is retransmitted (3 recommended, 5 is default)'
Info / Rationale: How many times unacknowledged data is retransmitted (3 recommended, 5 is default) in the SCE.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure TcpMaxDataRetransmissions is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes'
Description: 1.1.3.9.8 Configure 'MSS: (EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes'
Info / Rationale: It is recommended to configure this setting to Not Defined for enterprise environments and to Disabled for high security environments.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure EnableICMPRedirect is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (NoDefaultExempt) Configure IPSec exemptions for various types of network traffic.'
Description: 1.1.3.9.9 Configure 'MSS: (NoDefaultExempt) Configure IPSec exemptions for various types of network traffic.'
Info / Rationale: These filters make it possible for Internet Key Exchange (IKE) and the Kerberos authentication protocol to function.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure NoDefaultExempt is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (KeepAliveTime) How often keep-alive packets are sent in milliseconds'
Description: 1.1.3.9.10 Configure 'MSS: (KeepAliveTime) How often keep-alive packets are sent in milliseconds'
Info / Rationale: This value controls how often TCP attempts to verify that an idle connection is still intact by sending a keep-alive packet.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure KeepAliveTime is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (TcpMaxDataRetransmissions IPv6) How many times unacknowledged data is retransmitted (3 recommended, 5 default)'
Description: 1.1.3.9.11 Configure 'MSS: (TcpMaxDataRetransmissions IPv6) How many times unacknowledged data is retransmitted (3 recommended, 5 default)'
Info / Rationale:
Configure 'MSS: (TcpMaxDataRetransmissions IPv6) How many times unacknowledged data is retransmitted (3 recommended, 5 is default)'
How many times unacknowledged data is retransmitted (3 recommended, 5 is default) in the SCE.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure TcpMaxDataRetransmissions is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (NoNameReleaseOnDemand) Allow the computer to ignore NetBIOS name release requests except from WINS servers'
Description: 1.1.3.9.12 Configure 'MSS: (NoNameReleaseOnDemand) Allow the computer to ignore NetBIOS name release requests except from WINS servers'
Info / Rationale: This setting determines whether the computer releases its NetBIOS name when it receives a name-release request.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure NoNameReleaseOnDemand is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'MSS: (Hidden) Hide Computer From the Browse List (not recommended except for highly secure environments)'
Description: 1.1.3.9.13 Configure 'MSS: (Hidden) Hide Computer From the Browse List (not recommended except for highly secure environments)'
Info / Rationale: Hiding the computer from the browse list will not allow the computer to announce itself to other computers on the same network. You can enable this setting to remove one method that an attacker might use to gather information about computers on the network.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure Hidden is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'MSS: (ScreenSaverGracePeriod) The time in seconds before the screen saver grace period expires (0 recommended)' to '0'
Description: 1.1.3.9.14 Set 'MSS: (ScreenSaverGracePeriod) The time in seconds before the screen saver grace period expires (0 recommended)' to '0'
Info / Rationale: The time in seconds before the screen saver grace period expires (0 recommended) in the SCE.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure ScreenSaverGracePeriod is set to 0 seconds.

Title: Set 'MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting IPv6) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)' to 'Highest'
Description: 1.1.3.9.15 Set 'MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting IPv6) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)' to 'Highest'
Info / Rationale:
Set 'MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting IPv6) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)' to 'Highest protection, source routing is completely disabled'
IP source routing is a mechanism that allows the sender to determine the IP route that a datagram should follow
through the network.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure DisableIPSourceRouting is set to a value of Highest protection, source routing is completely disabled'

Title: Configure 'MSS: (PerformRouterDiscovery) Allow IRDP to detect and configure Default Gateway addresses (could lead to DoS)'
Description: 1.1.3.9.16 Configure 'MSS: (PerformRouterDiscovery) Allow IRDP to detect and configure Default Gateway addresses (could lead to DoS)'
Info / Rationale: This setting is used to enable or disable the Internet Router Discovery Protocol (IRDP).
Solution / Remediation: Make sure PerformRouterDiscovery is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.10.1 Set 'Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines what additional permissions are assigned for anonymous connections to the computer.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure EveryoneIncludesAnonymous is disabled.

Title: Set 'Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.10.2 Set 'Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether an anonymous user can request security identifier (SID)
attributes for another user.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation' is disabled.

Title: Set 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.10.3 Set 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting controls the ability of anonymous users to enumerate SAM accounts as well as shares.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' is enabled so this is not allowed.

Title: Configure 'Network access: Named Pipes that can be accessed anonymously'
Description: 1.1.3.10.4 Configure 'Network access: Named Pipes that can be accessed anonymously'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which communication sessions, or pipes, will have attributes and permissions that allow anonymous access.
NOTE: Update ANON_NAMED_PIPES with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure NullSessionPipes is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.10.5 Set 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
When enabled, this policy setting restricts anonymous access to only those shares and pipes that are named
in the Named pipes and Shares.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure restrictnullsessaccess is enabled.

Title: Set 'Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts' to 'Classic - local users authenticate as themselves'
Description: 1.1.3.10.6 Set 'Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts' to 'Classic - local users authenticate as themselves'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines how network logons that use local accounts are authenticated.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts' is set to classic.

Title: Set 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths and sub-paths' to the following list
Description: 1.1.3.10.7 Set 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths and sub-paths' to the following list
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which registry paths and sub-paths will be accessible when an application or
process references the WinReg key to determine access permissions.
Solution / Remediation:
Make sure Remotely accessible registry paths are set to 'System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Printers',
 'System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Eventlog',
 'Software\Microsoft\OLAP Server',
 'Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Print',
 'Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows',
 'System\CurrentControlSet\Control\ContentIndex',
 'System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server',
 'System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\UserConfig',
 'System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\DefaultUserConfiguration',
 'Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Perflib',
 'System\CurrentControlSet\Services\SysmonLog'.
Value Data: "System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Printers" && "System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Eventlog" && "Software\Microsoft\OLAP Server" && "Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Print" && "Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows" && "System\CurrentControlSet\Control\ContentIndex" && "System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server" && "System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\UserConfig" && "System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\DefaultUserConfiguration" && "Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Perflib" && "System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Sysmonlog"

Title: Configure Network access: Shares that can be accessed anonymously
Description: 1.1.3.11.3 Configure Network access: Shares that can be accessed anonymously
Info / Rationale:
NOTE: Update ANON_SHARE with the appropriate value for the local environment
This policy setting determines which network shares can be accessed by anonymous users.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure NullSessionShares is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths' to the following list
Description: 1.1.3.10.10 Set 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths' to the following list
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which registry paths will be accessible after referencing the WinReg key to determine access permissions to the paths.
Note: This setting does not exist in Windows XP. There was a setting with that name in Windows XP, but it is called 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths and subpaths' in Windows Server 2003, Windows Vista, and Windows Server 2008.
Note: When you configure this setting you specify a list of one or more objects. The delimiter used when entering the list is a line feed or carriage return, that is, type the first object on the list, press the Enter button, type the next object, press Enter again, etc. The setting value is stored as a comma-delimited list in group policy security templates. It is also rendered as a comma-delimited list in Group Policy Editor's display pane and the Resultant Set of Policy console. It is recorded in the registry as a line-feed delimited list in a REG_MULTI_SZ value. The recommended state for this setting is:
System\CurrentControlSet\Control\ProductOptions
System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Server Applications
Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion
Solution / Remediation:
To establish the recommended configuration via GP, set the following UI path to
System\CurrentControlSet\Control\ProductOptions
System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Server Applications
Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion.
Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths

Title: Configure 'Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication'
Description: 1.1.3.10.11 Configure 'Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether the Stored User Names and Passwords feature may save passwords or credentials for later use when it gains domain authentication.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure DisableDomainCreds is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.11.1 Set 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether the LAN Manager (LM) hash value for the new password is stored when
the password is changed.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' is enabled.

Title: Set 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based servers' to 'Require NTLMv2 session security'
Description: 1.1.3.11.2 Set 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based servers' to 'Require NTLMv2 session security'
Info / Rationale:
Set 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) servers' to 'Require NTLMv2 session security,Require 128-bit encryption'
This policy setting determines which behaviors are allowed for applications using the NTLM Security Support Provider.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients' is set to require NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption.

Title: Set 'Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.11.3 Set 'Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting causes Local System services that use Negotiate to use the computer identity when NTLM
authentication is selected by the negotiation.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM' is configured to 'Enabled'

Title: Set 'Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.11.4 Set 'Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: This control determines if a service is allowed to establish a NULL session connection.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback' is configured to 'Disabled'

Title: 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: NTLM authentication in this domain'
Description: 1.1.3.11.5 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: NTLM authentication in this domain'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows you to audit NTLM authentication in a domain from this domain controller.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Audit NTLM authentication in this domain' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Add server exceptions in this domain'
Description: 1.1.3.11.6 Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Add server exceptions in this domain'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows you to create an exception list of servers in this domain to which clients are allowed to use NTLM pass-through authentication.
NOTE: Update DOMAIN_SERVER with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Add server exceptions in this domain' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based clients' to 'Require NTLMv2 session security'
Description: 1.1.3.11.7 Set 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based clients' to 'Require NTLMv2 session security'
Info / Rationale:
Set 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients' to 'Require NTLMv2 session security,Require 128-bit encryption'
This policy setting determines which behaviors are allowed for applications using the NTLM Security Support Provider.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients' is set to require NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption.

Title: Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers'
Description: 1.1.3.11.8 Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows you to deny or audit outgoing NTLM traffic from this Windows 7 or this Windows Server 2008 R2 computer to any Windows remote server.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Add remote server exceptions for NTLM authentication'
Description: 1.1.3.11.9 Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Add remote server exceptions for NTLM authentication'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows you to create an exception list of remote servers to which clients are allowed to use NTLM authentication.
NOTE: Update REMOTE_SERVER with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Add remote server exceptions for NTLM authentication' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Audit Incoming NTLM Traffic' to 'Not Defined'
Description: 1.1.3.11.10 Set 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Audit Incoming NTLM Traffic' to 'Not Defined'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows you to audit incoming NTLM traffic.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Audit Incoming NTLM Traffic' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM'
Description: 1.1.3.11.11 Set 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM'
Info / Rationale:
LAN Manager (LM) is a family of early Microsoft client/server software that allows users to link personal
computers together on a single network.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' is set to send NTLMv2 response only and refuse LM and NTLM.

Title: Set 'Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requeststo this computer to use online identities' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.11.12 Set 'Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requeststo this computer to use online identities' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: The PKU2U protocol is a peer-to-peer authentication protocol. In most managed networks authentication should be managed centrally.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Audit NTLM authentication in this domain'
Description: 1.1.3.11.13 Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Audit NTLM authentication in this domain'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows you to audit NTLM authentication in a domain from this domain controller.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Audit NTLM authentication in this domain' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Incoming NTLM traffic'
Description: 1.1.3.11.14 Configure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Incoming NTLM traffic'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows you to deny or allow incoming NTLM traffic.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Restrict NTLM: Incoming NTLM traffic' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network Security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos' to 'RC4\AES128\AES256\Future types'
Description: 1.1.3.11.15 Set 'Network Security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos' to 'RC4\AES128\AES256\Future types'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows you to set the encryption types that Kerberos is allowed to use.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network Security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Network security: LDAP client signing requirements' to 'Negotiate signing'
Description: 1.1.3.11.16 Set 'Network security: LDAP client signing requirements' to 'Negotiate signing'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines the level of data signing that is requested on behalf of clients that
issue LDAP BIND requests.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network security: LDAP client signing requirements' is set to negotiate signing.

Title: Configure 'Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire'
Description: 1.1.3.11.17 Configure 'Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether to disconnect users who are connected to the local computer outside their user account's valid logon hours.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Recovery console: Allow automatic administrative logon' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.12.1 Set 'Recovery console: Allow automatic administrative logon' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: The recovery console is a command-line environment that is used to recover from system problems.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Recovery console: Allow automatic administrative logon' is disabled.

Title: Set 'Recovery console: Allow floppy copy and access to all drives and all folders' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.12.2 Set 'Recovery console: Allow floppy copy and access to all drives and all folders' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting makes the Recovery Console SET command available which allows you to set the following recovery
console environment variables: - AllowWildCards. Enables wildcard support for some commands (such as the DEL command).
- AllowAllPaths. Allows access to all files and folders on the computer. - AllowRemovableMedia. Allows files to be
copied to removable media, such as a floppy disk.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Recovery console: Allow floppy copy and access to all drives and all folders' is disabled.

Title: Set 'Shutdown: Clear virtual memory pagefile' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.13.1 Set 'Shutdown: Clear virtual memory pagefile' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether the virtual memory pagefile is cleared when the system is shut down.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Shutdown: Clear virtual memory pagefile' is disabled.

Title: Set 'Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.13.2 Set 'Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether a computer can be shut down when a user is not logged on.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on' is disabled.

Title: Configure 'System cryptography: Force strong key protection for user keys stored on the computer'
Description: 1.1.3.14.1 Configure 'System cryptography: Force strong key protection for user keys stored on the computer'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether users' private keys (such as their S-MIME keys) require a password to be used.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'System cryptography: Force strong key protection for user keys stored on the computer' is set to you organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'System cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.14.2 Set 'System cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines whether the Transport Layer Security/Secure Sockets Layer (TLS/SSL) Security Provider
supports only the TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA cipher.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'System cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing' is enabled.

Title: Set 'System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e'g' Symbolic Links)' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.15.1 Set 'System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e'g' Symbolic Links)' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines the strength of the default discretionary access control list (DACL) for objects.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects' is enabled.

Title: Set 'System objects: Require case insensitivity for nonWindows subsystems' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.15.2 Set 'System objects: Require case insensitivity for nonWindows subsystems' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether case insensitivity is enforced for all subsystems.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'System objects: Require case insensitivity for non-Windows subsystems' is enabled.

Title: Configure 'System settings: Optional subsystems'
Description: 1.1.3.16.1 Configure 'System settings: Optional subsystems'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which subsystems are used to support applications in your environment.
NOTE: Update OPT_SUBSYSTEMS with the appropriate value for the local environment
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'System settings: Optional subsystems' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.1 Set 'User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting controls the behavior of Admin Approval Mode for the built-in Administrator account.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account' is enabled.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.2 Set 'User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting controls the behavior of application installation detection for the computer.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation' is enabled.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users' to 'Automatically deny elevation requests'
Description: 1.1.3.17.3 Set 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users' to 'Automatically deny elevation requests'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting controls the behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Behavior of the Elevation Prompt for Standard Users' is set to Automatically deny elevation requests.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode' to 'Prompt for consent'
Description: 1.1.3.17.4 Set 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode' to 'Prompt for consent'
Info / Rationale:
Set 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode' to 'Prompt for consent on the secure desktop'
This policy setting controls the behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode' is set to 'Prompt for consent on the secure desktop'

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.5 Set 'User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting controls whether applications that request to run with a User Interface Accessibility
(UIAccess) integritylevel must reside in a secure location in the file system.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Only Elevate UIAccess applications that are Installed in Secure Locations' is Enabled.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.6 Set 'User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting controls whether application write failures are redirected to defined registry and
file system locations.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations' is enabled.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.7 Set 'User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting controls whether the elevation request prompt is displayed on the interactive user's desktop
or the secure desktop.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation' is enabled.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.8 Set 'User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting controls whether User Interface Accessibility (UIAccess or UIA) programs can automatically
disable the secure desktop for elevation prompts used by a standard user.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop' is disabled.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Only elevate executables that are signed and validated' to 'Disabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.9 Set 'User Account Control: Only elevate executables that are signed and validated' to 'Disabled'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting enforces public key infrastructure (PKI) signature checks for any interactive applications
that request elevation of privilege.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Only elevate executables that are signed and validated' is disabled.

Title: Set 'User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode' to 'Enabled'
Description: 1.1.3.17.10 Set 'User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode' to 'Enabled'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting controls the behavior of all User Account Control (UAC) policy settings for the computer.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode' is enabled.

Title: Configure 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services'
Description: 1.1.4.1 Configure 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines which users or groups have the right to log on as a Terminal Services client.
Solution / Remediation: Restrict this user right to the Administrators group, and possibly the Remote Desktop Users group, to prevent unwanted users from gaining access to computers on your network by means of the Remote Assistance feature.

Title: Set 'Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services' to 'Guests'
Description: 1.1.4.2 Set 'Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services' to 'Guests'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether users can log on as Terminal Services clients.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services' to 'Guests'.

Title: Set 'Deny access to this computer from the network' to 'Guests'
Description: 1.1.4.3 Set 'Deny access to this computer from the network' to 'Guests'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting prohibits users from connecting to a computer from across the network.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Deny access to this computer from the network' is set to guests.

Title: Set 'Create a pagefile' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.4 Set 'Create a pagefile' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows users to change the size of the pagefile.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Create a pagefile' is set to administrators.

Title: Set 'Create permanent shared objects' to 'No One'
Description: 1.1.4.5 Set 'Create permanent shared objects' to 'No One'
Info / Rationale: This user right is useful to kernel-mode components that extend the object namespace.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Create permanent shared objects' is set to No One.

Title: Set 'Increase scheduling priority' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.6 Set 'Increase scheduling priority' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether users can increase the base priority class of a process.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Increase scheduling priority' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Access this computer from the network' to 'Users, Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.7 Set 'Access this computer from the network' to 'Users, Administrators'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows other users on the network to connect to the computer and is required by various
network protocols that include Server Message Block (SMB)-based protocols, NetBIOS, Common Internet File System (CIFS),
and Component Object Model Plus (COM+).
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Access this computer from the network' is set to administrators and usersllers.

Title: Set 'Force shutdown from a remote system' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.8 Set 'Force shutdown from a remote system' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows users to shut down Windows Vista-based computers from remote locations on the network.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Force shutdown from a remote system' is set to administrators.

Title: Set 'Change the time zone' to 'LOCAL SERVICE, Administrators, Users'
Description: 1.1.4.9 Set 'Change the time zone' to 'LOCAL SERVICE, Administrators, Users'
Info / Rationale: This setting determines which users can change the time zone of the computer.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Change the time zone' is set to local service, administrators, and users.

Title: Set 'Create global objects' to 'Administrators, SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE'
Description: 1.1.4.10 Set 'Create global objects' to 'Administrators, SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines whether users can create global objects that are available to all sessions.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Create global objects' is set to administrators, service, local service and network service.

Title: Set 'Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation' to 'No One'
Description: 1.1.4.11 Set 'Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation' to 'No One'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows users to change the Trusted for Delegation setting on a computer object in Active Directory.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation' is set to no one.

Title: Set 'Profile single process' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.12 Set 'Profile single process' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines which users can use tools to monitor the performance of non-system processes.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Profile single process' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Shut down the system' to 'Administrators, Users'
Description: 1.1.4.13 Set 'Shut down the system' to 'Administrators, Users'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines which users can shut down the operating system with the Shut Down command.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Shut down the system' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Take ownership of files or other objects' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.14 Set 'Take ownership of files or other objects' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows users to take ownership of files, folders, registry keys, processes, or threads.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Take ownership of files or other objects' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Create symbolic links' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.15 Set 'Create symbolic links' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines which users can create symbolic links.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Create symbolic links' is set to administrators.

Title: Set 'Act as part of the operating system' to 'No One'
Description: 1.1.4.16 Set 'Act as part of the operating system' to 'No One'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows a process to assume the identity of any user and thus gain access to the resources that
the user is authorized to access.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure no one can act as part of the operating system.

Title: Set 'Modify firmware environment values' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.17 Set 'Modify firmware environment values' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows users to configure the system-wide environment variables that affect hardware configuration.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Modify firmware environment values' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Back up files and directories' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.18 Set 'Back up files and directories' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows users to circumvent file and directory permissions to back up the system.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Back up files and directories' is set to administrators.

Title: Debug programs = Administrators
Description: 1.1.4.19 Debug programs = Administrators
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which user accounts will have the right to attach a debugger to any process
or to the kernel.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Debug programs' is set to administrators only.

Title: Set 'Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller' to 'No One'
Description: 1.1.4.20 Set 'Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller' to 'No One'
Info / Rationale: This security setting is used by Credential Manager during Backup and Restore.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Access Credential Manager as a trusted caller' is set no one.

Title: Set 'Deny log on locally' to 'Guests'
Description: 1.1.4.21 Set 'Deny log on locally' to 'Guests'
Info / Rationale: This security setting determines which users are prevented from logging on at the computer.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Deny log on locally' is set to guest accounts only.

Title: Set 'Profile system performance' to 'NT SERVICE\WdiServiceHost,Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.22 Set 'Profile system performance' to 'NT SERVICE\WdiServiceHost,Administrators'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows users to use tools to view the performance of different system processes,
which could be abused to allow attackers to determine a system's active processes and provide insight
into the potential attack surface of the computer.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Profile system performance' is set to Administrators and NT SERVICE\WdiServiceHost.

Title: Set 'Restore files and directories' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.23 Set 'Restore files and directories' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which users can bypass file, directory, registry, and other persistent object permissions
when restoring backed up files and directories on computers that run Windows Vista in your environment.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Restore files and directories' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Perform volume maintenance tasks' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.24 Set 'Perform volume maintenance tasks' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows users to manage the system's volume or disk configuration, which could allow a user
to delete a volume and cause data loss as well as a denial-of-service condition.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Perform volume maintenance tasks' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Impersonate a client after authentication' to 'Administrators, SERVICE, Local Service, Network Service'
Description: 1.1.4.25 Set 'Impersonate a client after authentication' to 'Administrators, SERVICE, Local Service, Network Service'
Info / Rationale:
The policy setting allows programs that run on behalf of a user to impersonate that user so that they can act
on behalf of the user.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Impersonate a client after authentication' is set to Administrators, SERVICE, Local Service and Network Service.

Title: Configure 'Log on as a batch job'
Description: 1.1.4.26 Configure 'Log on as a batch job'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows accounts to log on using the task scheduler service.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Log on as a Batch Job' is set to your organization's security policy.

Title: Set 'Adjust memory quotas for a process' to 'Administrators, Local Service, Network Service'
Description: 1.1.4.27 Set 'Adjust memory quotas for a process' to 'Administrators, Local Service, Network Service'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting allows a user to adjust the maximum amount of memory that is available to a process.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Adjust memory quotas for a process' is set to administrators, local service and network service.

Title: Set 'Manage auditing and security log' to 'Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.28 Set 'Manage auditing and security log' to 'Administrators'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting determines which users can change the auditing options for files and directories and clear
the Security log.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Manage auditing and security log' is set to Administrators.

Title: Set 'Deny log on as a batch job' to 'Guests'
Description: 1.1.4.29 Set 'Deny log on as a batch job' to 'Guests'
Info / Rationale: This policy setting determines which accounts will not be able to log on to the computer as a batch job.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Deny log on as a batch job' is set to guests.

Title: Set 'Bypass traverse checking' to 'Users, NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE, Administrators'
Description: 1.1.4.30 Set 'Bypass traverse checking' to 'Users, NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE, Administrators'
Info / Rationale:
This policy setting allows users who do not have the Traverse Folder access permission to pass through folders
when they browse an object path in the NTFS file system or the registry.
Solution / Remediation: Make sure 'Bypass traverse checking' is set to authenticated users, administrators, local service, and network service.

Title: Set 'Increase a process working set' to 'Administrators, Local Service'
Description: 1.1.4.31 Set 'Increase a process working set' to 'Administrators, Local Service'
